problem: Consider the arc of the curve $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ that lies between the lines $x=0$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ What integral gives the area of the surface generated when this arc is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi x\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since we're given a curve in the form $y=f(x),$ we have 

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}x\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}x\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\sqrt{1+(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
